To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combined application of moderate rates cattle manure and fertilizer (i.e., ISFM) can increase maize yield and nutrient use efficiency by up to 50% relative to sole manure or sole fertilizer application.
the combination of cattle manure with inorganic fertilizer in smallholder farming systems of SSA is a promising approach to increase nutrient and water use efficiencies and maize yields.
ISFM improves crop yield, rain use ef ciency, AEN and APF, but the magnitude of improvement depends on the manure and fertilizer rates applied.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of manure as an input to crop production in sub Saharan African smallholder farms.
improving crop yields, water and nutrient use efficiencies in smallholder farming systems in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA).
the development of a new generation of fertilizer management technologies for smallholder farmers in Africa.

the combined application of moderate rates (5 10t ha 1) of cattle manure with moderate rates (50kg N ha 1 ) of inorganic fertilizer in maize production systems in SSA can increase grain yield by 50%, increase RUE and AEN and AEN by 100%, and reduce the amount of inorganic N required to achieve the same maize yield by 75% relative to sole application of cattle.
ISFM is a promising approach for smallholder farmers in SSA to increase maize yields and AEN.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined use of cattle manure with inorganic fertilizer is a promising strategy to improve maize yield response and nutrient use efficiency in SSA.

the combined application of moderate cattle manure rates and moderate N fertilizer rates can significantly improve agronomic efficiency of N fertilizer application and crop yield response in SSA maize production systems.

the combined application of moderate rates (5 10t ha 1) of cattle manure with moderate doses (50kg N ha 1 and 20kg P ha 1) N and P fertilizer, respectively, is the most efficient way to improve maize yields on responsive soils.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combined application of moderate rates (5 10t ha 1) of cattle manure with inorganic fertilizer is a more efficient way of increasing maize yield and N and P use efficiency in SSA.
